newsitem.title: GERMANY: German tax reform creates new gaps in budgets.
newsitem.headline: German tax reform creates new gaps in budgets.

text.p: The German government's tax reform proposals that will be phased in over the next two years will create an additional financing gap in the federal budget of 731 million marks in 1998, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.

The measures, aimed at creating a net income tax reduction of up to 30 billion marks, will create an additional financing gap in the federal budget of 20.601 billion marks in 1999. The gap for the combined federal, state and local budgets will be 44.941 billion marks, the ministry said.

The ministry made clear in a statement distributed in Bonn after a meeting of parliament's finance committee that the tax reform would create an additional financing gap for the regional state budgets of 494 million marks in 1998.

Changes to the tax structure that would make it more difficult for companies to lower tax burdens by carrying losses forward into profitable years and new rules to affect hidden reserves would cost industry some four billion marks in 1998, it said.

The changes to taxes on hidden reserves are widely expected to have a particular impact on energy companies, which have stockpiled huge sums as a precautionary move in the event of any accident at nuclear power plants.

Of the four billion marks, around 1.986 billion marks would flow into public budgets as a result of a new rule forbidding companies from building reserves for the purpose of covering production and purchasing costs.
Changes to rules on carrying forward losses would raise another 1.282 billion marks in tax revenue for public budgets.
The additional financing gap comes on top of a projected federal budget deficit of 53.3 billion marks this year and 58 billion marks next year.

The government has indicated that both of these forecasts will have to be revised when the financial planning council of budget experts from federal, state and local governments and the Bundesbank meet on June 25.
